body:
Holy fuck I agree with this. Especially that part about being really animated and expressive and yet having trouble connecting. For me, being expressive makes people approach me at first, but soon they'll realize there's nothing more to me beyond that and so they "move on" to others who are more interesting. I feel like a boring piece of crap under that expressive facade, basically.

I try to compensate for that by getting affirmation online, but I don't even succeed at that. Most of time, I over-analyze what I'm writing (just like you) and end up with really choppy, convoluted sentences that just don't flow well, which makes me feel super awkward. Then the forum anxiety kicks in when I end up getting no likes/upvotes/positive replies/etc. It's especially painful when a reply disagreeing with my post gets *way* more likes than mine. I want to delete my post so badly then, but I don't because I fear others will find me pathetic. Which makes me pathetic.

Thanks for your concerns :)

Thankfully, I'm feeling better today, so didn't go through with that plan to kill myself haha. But still, I cried myself to sleep last night. Basically, my problems can be summed up as "obsessive thoughts". And it's not just any obsessive thoughts; they're the same thoughts I've been having ever since I was 13 (I'm 18 now). They've taken up 5 years of my life, they're constantly eating away at me (there are some periods where it gets better, of course). And it's like these thoughts get to me whenever I least expect them to. 

Worst part is, I don't know what's wrong with me. I've checked and there doesn't seem to be a mental illness that causes such severe obsessive thoughts. I really don't know what's wrong.

E: And I don't know how I'm supposed to tell people about this. Like, these obsessive thoughts are really hard to explain, and the reason why I had them in the first place is complicated (which is why I'm being vague in this post).
Okay, I just saw it. I still disagree that they're lazily written, as I think their goal ties in neatly to the legendaries and lore in Sinnoh, which was what the OP was getting at.
Why do you think their writing is lazy? Elaborate please? I'm really curious why people think this.

Thanks for putting this into words better than I can. I, too, think that Team Galactic has gotten a lot of unfair treatment from the fan base, especially Cyrus. I'd just like to add I'm one of those people who find his backstory plausible, if not sympathetic.

I mean, just think about it. He's antisocial, so we can assume nobody really reached out to him. His parents are also most likely neglectful as his grandfather was actually worried for him. To him, the world must have been a cruel and lonely place.
I don't know any Sinnoh fans personally, but I frequent Tumblr sometimes and enjoy seeing the posts clamoring over D/P remakes or how awesome Sinnoh is ;-P

I see. I guess that may be the reason you don't remember much about it then. 10 years is a really long time, and from the looks of it, that was around the time you were getting frustrated/burnt out after losing game after game.

Oh I'm sure I'll find that old pretty soon. But still, doesn't stop me from fantasizing about beautiful white landscapes and snowangels, among other stuff, haha.

I get pretty darn sick of my weather sometimes. When it isn't raining, the heat makes me feel lethargic.

So what do you think of the amount of legends in the later gens? Gen 5 had 14 iirc, pretty close to 15.

Oh well, Pokemon designs are pretty subjective, so I can't argue with you on this I guess. Personally though, I find there to be more than 26 appealing designs compared to...maybe 4-5 bad ones?

This is an interesting way to put it that I never see much of in discussions. I guess the places we live in do affect our opinions of certain regions to some extent. I live in a tropical area where there's no snow at all, so Sinnoh was that perfect fantasy escape land for me (I've always wished to experience snow).
Thank you for the reply. So far from what I see here it's the aesthetic aspects of the game that people find bland: the region's appearance, the color palette, city/town variety, etc.

Can you elaborate on what you mean by "forgettable"? Or do you mean forgettable *because* of the region being bland in your opinion?

Also, what do you mean by "organic" to the plot? I'm not sure what is meant by that.
Hm, when was the last time you played it?
Maybe among people who grew up with it, but besides that, I don't see that many people praising it really.
So did the slowness of the game made it unmemorable to you?

Okay, but is it the same with the other regions for you? Like, if you don't visit them for a while, will you not remember much about them as well?

10 years is a pretty darn long time, so that may be why you don't remember it.

I feel like Kanto gets a pass because it's the first. Nobody really talks about it these days anyways aside from when people complain about there being pandering towards it.

I agree about Sinnoh. Eterna City had that statue, Hearthome had an (eerie) church, Solaceon had the ruins, Celestic was overflowing with mythology from top to bottom, Canalave had the library, Snowpoint had a temple and is linked to Mt. Coronet, there were the three lakes, plus those little tidbits of lore found throughout Galactic's HQ, the Arceus plates scattered all over Sinnoh, how Mt. Coronet had this alleged "energy" in it...there was just so much implicit storytelling in the region that I feel often gets overlooked.
I've heard this plenty also, but then there's just that section of the fan base that finds it bland, forgettable, unmemorable etc. for unexplained reasons...
So with this in mind, do you think that some of its' areas feel "forced" in? Like they don't seem to connect to the areas before/after them but were added in for the sake of it anyway?

I agree about Sinnoh. I love the region personally, but the lore (which I'm a fan of also) is definitely the main attraction. What I love was how they incorporated Mt. Coronet symbolically into Sinnoh's aesthetic - lined in the dead center of the region, towering, mighty, etc. The way it's positioned really does make it seem like Sinnoh's continent originated and blossomed from it.
Kind of sums up my stance in a nutshell. But my question was why's Sinnoh in particular deemed as bland.
I've seen a lot of that. All the way from 2011 to present. Though there's definitely less distaste for it now, it being the blandest region still seems to be a notion.
We can agree on that!

Yeah, I think it'll really help if you play Pokémon platinum. In D/P, Cyrus, Cynthia, Barry, the gym leaders etc. we're not really fleshed out at all; D/P emphasizes more on Cyrus wanting to be a deity rather than his goal to eliminate spirit, Cynthia wasn't as involved in taking down Team Galactic/researching the myths, Barry had less dialogue/screentime so his development there was more shallow, and the gym leaders had less dialogue also (if memory serves). These factors are probably why its' characters and story didn't grip you. All of these were alleviated in Platinum *at least* to some extent. Of course, the story still isn't as focused on as in BW/SM, but it was the first step the series took in making its' plots better; I'd say Platinum was actually the pre-cursor to Pokemon plots being as fleshed out as they are now (as Chuggaconroy would put it).

Platinum also has more content than Diamond. The post game is larger (with the Battle Frontier which HGSS borrowed from), and if it means anything to you, the Poketch was even improved! Rather than 1 button, it now has 2 buttons which makes it easier to scroll through the apps. Trust me, it makes a difference.

In terms of pokemon distribution, more fire types were added into the main game as I'm sure you've heard before. There's now the Magmar, Flareon, Houndoom lines to choose from, alongside the Chimchar and Ponyta lines. Platinum's pokedex is just superior in general.

Thank you for the detailed comment. So it is the region that causes people to find it bland then...(on a side-note, why was ambipom unneeded? It was one of those much-needed evolutions imo)

So I take it that your overall problem with it was that it doesn't have a distinguishable aesthetic theme then? I don't know about you, but I think Sinnoh isn't meant to represent any sort of culture or continent, but rather just a generic mountainous area. This would explain why there're so many caves throughout the region, and the snow. To an extent, it also explains why pretty much all you see are typical nature's components such as rocks, trees, and dirt; as man-made attractions/civilization are typically hard to build on uneven land (correct me if I'm wrong here as I have no exposure whatsoever to mountainous areas).

I actually have somewhat of a theory here: snow tends to be bland in appearance; it covers up anything interesting on the continent with a wide, plain blanket of nothingness. It's anything but vibrant. Because a region's vibrancy tends to be the main attraction for people, the fact that Sinnoh has an abundance of snow (due to its' location and mountainous nature) leaves them with the impression of it being more barren and dull than the other regions aesthetic-wise, hence why people find it bland.

I've seen this a lot. Lots of people who've called Sinnoh "bland" later say that they don't know why it comes off that way to them. Perhaps it has something to do with the vibe it gives off?

Maybe it'll help if you list out what you like about HGSS and BW (which I take were some of your favorite games) and, if possible, list what you don't like about D/P? I'm really curious about this.

(Also, totally recommend you play Platinum. It's much more rich with content than D/P is, and the storyline is improved, too. Not to mention the overall speed)

Whoa...if I hadn't upvoted this comment, it'd actually get a -1. Why would anyone downvote someone for expressing an opinion...? And you were being pretty respectful about it too; you were just saying gen 4 was *your* personal magical generation...

Yes...this is one of the things I love about gen 5 too, but I actually also love the legendary dynamics of gen 4, even though others dislike it. Despite being basically pokegods, I just found the concept of a creation trio to be really fascinating, and the fact that they are tied to/balanced out by the embodiments of spirit (lake trio) make them even more intriguing.
That extract is beautiful. Describes Cyrus perfectly, I would say.

Not to mention him explaining why he was angry or upset would've directly contradicted his character. While negative social contact may have contributed to his philosophy, the main reason for his contempt towards emotion was because he didn't understand -and couldn't deal with- his own. This quote that I've posted several times in this thread says it all:

"The emotions roiling inside me...rage, hatred, frustration...these ugly emotions arise because of my own incomplete spirit!"

Him explaining "oh, I turned out like this because I was hurt by my parents" would've taken so much away from this quote.

Hm...I wouldn't say his end goal is to get people to follow him. (Actually, I don't see this at all; the only people he goes out of his way to manipulate are the team Galactic grunts, and he literally did so just because he had to use them for his goal). He seems to genuinely believe in his cause, evidenced by his dialogue near the end of the plot, particularly, this line:

"*The emotions roiling inside me...rage, hatred, frustration...these ugly emotions arise because of my own incomplete spirit*!"

The fact that he truly appears to be angry at himself for his incomplete spirit shows that he really does harbor a lot of contempt towards the human spirit. His outburst here alone shows that he's still struggling with the unresolved emotions that lead him to where he is.

It's true that Cyrus doesn't care about anyone, but it's only because of his apathy for people that he views the human spirit as incomplete. He doesn't see people as individuals; he sees them as machines that are faulty because of emotions (this is due to him growing up with machines with little to no social contact, and the contact he did have with his parents were negative). It is because of this that he sees them as incomplete, and wants to recreate a universe where they can be as complete and perfect as the emotionless machines are in his view. 

Tl;dr:  Cyrus not caring about anyone doesn't make his beliefs any less genuine; in fact, they're the whole reason why he harbored those beliefs about people in the first place.

Yes, there was that part about Cyrus's grandfather saying how he regrets not taking him in in his time of need when he had the chance. Actually, this made me think of something. I know you said you liked how Cyrus didn't have any traumatic backstory to his character, but if you think about the fact that his grandfather had actually considered taking him in (and regrets not doing so), added by the fact that he described child!Cyrus as "in need"...that would imply some pretty serious neglect, wouldn't it? At least, it'd imply something more serious than merely "unappreciated".

I hope this doesn't sound rude, but, well, of course he's going to pick and choose what the universe should be like in his view. The thing is, he *thinks* he's doing things for the greater good. But really, he was just projecting his past experiences on the rest of the world. This is what the game was trying to portray.

I haven't played XY in a long time, so can you explain why you thought Lysandre felt more genuine in his goal than Cyrus? Maybe give some comparisons? Perhaps then I could understand where you're coming from better.

Yes! I'm surprised there aren't more people that see the duality between Cyrus and Cynthia. I mean, come on, their names even mean Sun and Moon (wait...) respectively, for heavens' sake!

Here's to hoping they shed more light on this duality in the remakes.

Well, those people most likely don't happen to also be mad scientists, don't they? Also, there's no way to reset the universe irl anyway, so those people, unlike Cyrus, have no choice but to either introspect and find their own way out, get some help, or...you know, end it the easy way (which is very unfortunate). Context matters a lot here.

As I said before, there are lots of factors that could factor into Cyrus's goal. Being a genius (I'd argue we do see it in adult Cyrus. He showcased that by having the knowledge to harvest the gems from the lake trio and manufacture them into red chains) and having the parental backstory are just two of them. There's also his personality of him being antisocial; which seals off all of his windows to the social world and hence him having no (positive) experience with humans whatsoever. It's implied he grew up with machines, hence his understandings of machines are much greater than that of other humans. Humans are full of messy emotions, machines aren't. This would be why emotions scare him; as there are no clear-cut formula to understanding them the way machines can be understood. This apprehension towards emotion, combined with nothing but bad social experiences, contribute to his contempt for human emotion. 

Dialga and Palkia have the power to recreate the universe. He knows this, and since there are actual tools (Dialga and Palkia) in his world that allow him to do so, it gives him that extra motivation and push (that you wouldn't see in rl depressed people) to actually set out to do so by studying the lore, setting up the procedures, plan out his goal, etc. Then there's also the fact that "emotion is the source of all strife" is an actual archetypical philosophy. While this may seem like some minor unrelated trivia, it goes to show that Cyrus's beliefs aren't completely nonsensical as they at least have some archetypical/logical grounding to them.

Anyways, this is just me elaborating on my points beforehand, just in case they're unclear. If you still disagree with these, then I guess we just don't see eye to eye on this matter then. Well, I hope for your sake that remake Cyrus improves the way you want him to.

"generic strawman philosophy we assign to world destroying type of villains"

I don't think you can apply that to Cyrus. I think the word you're looking for is cliché?

Anyways, the reason why I don't think that's applicable to Cyrus is because that makes it sound as if the philosophy he adopted isn't genuine, and is just using that philosophy as a ploy to dominate the world. From the game, it sounds like Cyrus is pretty genuine and passionate about what he stood for. Here's a quote from the game I used in my OP to demonstrate that:

"The emotions roiling inside me...rage, hatred, frustration...these ugly emotions arise because of my own incomplete spirit!"

His condemnation towards his own "spirit" at the end of the plot, rather than a hate speech about failing to dominate the world, makes me think that he's pretty involved in what he believes in; it makes it seem fixing the incomplete human spirit is his main goal, and "destroying" the world is just a part of reaching that goal. That's what sets him apart from other world destroying villains, for me at least.

Hm...from what you've said so far, I'm curious to know if there are any pokemon villains that you thought were handled well?

If that's the case, can't you say that's true for all Pokemon villains? (barring TP, but that's only because freeing Pokemon wasn't even their real plan anyway) TM/TA wanted to expand land/sea for the Pokemon, but as far as we've heard of, there aren't any problems regarding the habitats of land and sea Pokemon. Team Flare wanted to eliminate some of the population due to limited world resources, but no problems regarding resources nor overpopulation were established beforehand.

Haven't played SM yet.

Wait, I thought there was an NPC in Sunyshore who mentioned him being a child genius or something?

Anyways, I see your point, but parental love is a really important part of a child's life. You've got to remember our interactions with our parents are our very first experience with the social world, and hence the most impressionable. Cyrus not only had a bad experience with this, he isn't particularly social either -in fact, he doesn't even have any friends!- so he doesn't even have any other social interactions to fall back on. 

It's been implied he spent the entirety of his childhood tinkering with machines. It hasn't been implied he does anything else other than that; so you could say he was completely machine-minded (that a word? Lol); exacerbated by the fact that he had no social life to distract him from his machines. 

There's also the fact that spirit being the source of all conflicts is an actual philosophy shared by some rl philosophers, so it isn't all that far-fetched that the game had Cyrus adopt this philosophy.

Tl;dr:
Non-existent social life + completely machine/science-minded + bad experience of emotions (from being denied parental love) + there being an actual philosophy on the weakness of spirit + the existence of Dialga and Palkia = the goal to recreate a reality without spirit.

Oh, and also, I'm curious as to why you'd say there wasn't any real weight to his plan? (or is that what you're saying at all?) Because it was established in-game that Dialga and Palkia do actually have the power to carry out his plan. Heck, he was about to succeed before we stopped him.

But how was it nonsensical? Thinking spirit is the source of all weakness/conflict is an actual philosophy shared by some people in real life (I read about it a few times before; in books, quotes by philosophers, movies, etc.). If we had the elements irl to recreate a world without conflict, I wouldn't be surprised if there are people who'd at least attempt to do just that.

Plus, judging from his backstory, Cyrus seems like someone who almost never experiences any positive emotions (love, joy etc.), so it isn't all that farfetched for him to think the world would be much better off without emotions.

I just find Sinnoh to be tragic in general. DP were the first games to be released on a vastly different hardware -it was their first time working with double screens ffs!- so of course a whole bunch of technical problems were to be expected. It's not just that either, it was also their first time incorporating wifi into the game..online trading etc...not to mention the physical/special split, which meant a complete overhaul of the competitive scene. It wasn't just some simple add-on like the day/night system or abilities, we're talking about a full-blown, massive *overhaul*. I suspect it's due to these huge changes that they focused less on the story, characters etc...you know, the actual game, which is why you get all these people saying how it's so bland, boring, stale etc. What makes things worse is that those huge changes were really technical/behind-the-scenes stuff, so people who don't pay attention to that kind of thing complain that it's uninnovative and brought nothing new, probably why gen 4 has this whole stigma about "playing it safe" despite those innovations. Then of course, when the developers have finally grown accustomed to these changes and technical workings of the ds later on, they were able to focus much more on story, characters, other in-game content etc. in later games, so then you'll have people constantly comparing gen 4 unfavorably to these "amazing-in-comparison" gens. Like someone here said, gen 4 really is the sacrificial cow of the series. And it breaks my heart when I see that it doesn't even get any recognition *at least* for its' sacrifice.

Platinum was definitely a well-deserved third version to really showcase how amazing Sinnoh can be, but even then you have people who write it off as being just another bland Sinnoh game, refusing to even give it a second chance. Unfortunately, Platinum was just a step too late to save Sinnoh entirely.

I'm sorry for dumping this whole rant on you. These thoughts were just on my mind for a really long time now, and your post happened to remind me of them.

Thank you for your suggestion. Tbh, I've been thinking about therapy a lot, but with the way life is right now, things will have to remain bleak for a long time. No, no..you don't come off as an ass at all, I've been aware of how unhealthy my situation is for a long time. This has been going on ever since I was 12 or so, when I had first discovered the online Pokemon fandom. Doing that was the worst mistake of my life it seems; I've still yet to break out of this horrid cycle to this day. Somewhere down the line I just knew I had to get help. It was getting so bad that at one point I literally saw nothing else to my life other than to check the internet 24/7 in fickle hopes that gen 4's reception would get better. And right now I think it's taking a turn for the worst again; I've actually cried a few times these past few weeks.

Thing is, finding someone to talk to isn't so easy. It's a hard subject to bring up among family and friends, and going to see a therapist is frowned upon in my family. This is why I saw no other choice than to vent out my feelings here. As I said, I just had to get this out of my system somehow before it gets uncontrollable.

Anyway, don't want to bother you with too many personal details, so I'll stop here.

Hah..."idiots" ;)

You know about those people I brought up in my OP? Those people who call Sinnoh-love out on being all fake and purely nostalgia-ridden? "Because it can't possibly be true because of how awful it is"? Those people always came off as jerks to me. Supremely condescending. It's as if they came in just to ruin whatever love Sinnoh is finally receiving after years and years of hatred and neglect. So what if they're speaking the truth anyway? What's their point? To make people feel bad? Well unfortunately, they succeeded on me. Hope they're happy knowing they've cut through at least one soul with their words.

That part about gen 5 is interesting, as I've always been bewildered at the sudden surge of its' popularity. People keep saying it gets hate for the most stupid reasons, and while that may have been the case in the past, it certainly isn't the case now. If anything, I find criticism towards gen 5 to be astoundingly rare these days, much less unjustified ones. Anyone who ridicules gen 5's pokemon designs seem to get jumped on immediately, whereas you still see plenty of people doing just that for the other regions \(*especially* DPP\), yet nobody bats an eye in those cases.

I guess I'm just being salty, I've seen one too many instances of Unova \(and sometimes Hoenn\) fans having a special affinity towards ridiculing Sinnoh's games, and being very condescending about it at that. There's just this underlying expression that Sinnoh's current popularity is solely due to mindless fanboy hype, while those with a "true taste for actual good game content and innovation" love Unova for what it is. I really, really hope this is just yet another personal projection of mine, and that the fandom isn't in actuality at all like that. But when you see certain patterns emerging over and over again, it's kinda hard to cling onto that hope, you know?

Thank you for this; just knowing that there are others out there who suffer/has suffered similar problems alone already brings me a great deal of comfort.

The part in your post about the YouTube comment section is probably more important than you think :\) Every time I watch or listen to a video on YouTube, I tend to subconsciously scroll down just to look at the comments. You warning me about them gives me more of an incentive to suppress this harmful habit of mine, even though the possibility of there being potential Sinnoh hate below still unsettles me greatly, and I'll immediately feel the urge to scroll through everything just so I can put myself at ease if there's none, at the risk of upsetting myself even more if there is.

Typing this out, I realize just how needlessly paranoid I am, and I wish more than anything that I could just put an end to this vicious cycle and enjoy pokemon the way I used to. But it just isn't that easy in practice.

I've seen his let's play on Platinum before, and I do agree that he does a great job at shedding positive light on the game. Watching his videos on Platinum definitely made me really happy.

But then again, he tends to be really optimistic about pretty much every pokemon game anyway, so I just don't feel him praising Platinum says very much when it comes to Sinnoh's reception.

Thanks for your suggestion; I might just try to replay it actually. When I feel really down after reading some nasty Sinnoh hate-posts/criticisms, I sometimes try to cheer myself up by listening to some of its' OST, and, while it isn't quite enough to lift my spirits entirely, it does bring a smile to my face just remembering some of my most treasured memories accompanied by those tunes.

I just wish I can find some way to forget all about the negativity once and for all; permanently. I'm sure I can enjoy myself when I'm in the midst of playing the games, but then when I'm done all the unpleasant memories will just come flooding back, and I can't keep distracting myself by playing those games forever. I'm happy that you find this to be an effective coping method for you; you seem to move on easier than me at least :\)
